name: 050_oi_flush_reversal_tf30
hypothesis: PLAN.md section 14, idea M1 (new data: open interest). A liquidation cascade shows up as a large price move over a few hours while open interest FALLS sharply: positions are being closed into the move, and at that speed most of them are forced (margin calls, the liquidation engine's market orders), not chosen. Forced flow is price-insensitive, so it pushes price past where voluntary traders would take it; when the forced sellers (buyers) are exhausted, price reverts over the next days. Counterparty: the liquidated traders and the engine selling their positions. Rule: over 4 bars, price z-score beyond -price_z (a down-flush) with OI z-score below -oi_z -> long; the mirror (price up, OI down = shorts squeezed out) -> short. z-scores are against each series' own last 720 bars (30 days at 1h). In a falling market this still trades both ways: it buys capitulation lows and sells short-squeeze spikes, and the short-squeeze side is the one that should work in a decline. Held 2-6 days (LESSONS.md section 1: multi-day holds are the only ones that pay for cost). Grid: how large an OI drop counts as a flush, and the hold. [Timeframe variant of 050_oi_flush_reversal, 60m -> 30m, mode chart: same bar counts and ATR multiples, hold x0.5, pct stop x0.707.]
